Figure 1. 3-NPA is a lethal mycotoxin. (A) Mycotoxins with
relevance to human health and identified BGC. (B) The proposed
biosynthesis of 1 in plants starting from malonic acid. (C) The
bacterial pathway of nitrite production through (S)-nitrosuccinic acid.
(D) The proposed biosynthesis of 1 via (S)-nitrosuccinic acid.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Biosynthesis of 1 by a dedicated biosynthetic gene cluster in fungi. (A) Putative BGCs of 1 are not only found in all known producers of
1 such as A. oryzae and A. saccharicola but also in fungi not reported to produce 1, such as P. nalgiovense and M. robertsii (see the Supporting
Information). (B) LC/MS detection of 3-NPH-1 from A. oryzae WT and abolished detection in the npaA-KO strain. (C) The synthetic scheme of
3-NPH-1 using EDC as the condensation reagent.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Biochemical characterization of NpaA, NpaB, and mr-NpaC. (A) In vitro characterization of NpaA and NpaB. (B) Detection of nitrite
from the in vitro reaction of mr-NpaC with 1. Pinkish color in the wells represents the detection of nitrite by the Griess reaction. (C) The proposed
biosynthetic and degradation pathway of 1.
